device.manufacturer: Hangzhou Daniao Technology Co., Ltd (SmartDawn/Minetom store brand)
device.name: SmartDawn Smart Lights
device.notes:
SmartDawn (smartdawn.com, Shopify storefront linked to the Minetom string-lights seller) sells addressable-RGB holiday lighting: RGBIC permanent outdoor string lights, icicle/net/curtain lights, meteor-shower tubes, cone trees. The products are white-label builds of Hangzhou Daniao Technology's "point-controlled color light" platform — the same stack behind Daniao's SuperPix (com.daniaokeji.cs) and legacy SmartPixel apps.
COMPANION APP: "SmartDawn" — Android com.daniaokeji.smartdawn (v1.2.4, updated 2026-01-06), iOS id 6749049089. Features: music/mic reactive modes, hand-drawn patterns, scrolling text, photo-to-light, groups, timers. Local BLE control works without any account or cloud.
PROTOCOL: custom "DDP/DNX" stack, mapped from decompilation of the official SmartDawn.apk v1.2.4 (jadx: com.daniaokeji.libs.bluetooth. BleUtils5, com.daniaokeji.libs.udp.*) cross-checked against the app's bundled H5 JavaScript (assets/HTML/assets/index-CL_jUmAY.js), which implements the same encoders a second time, and the app's bundled protobuf schema (assets/HTML/p2p.proto), which pins every message type number and payload shape. Commands are protobuf messages wrapped in a 20-byte extended DDP header, fragmented into BLE writes carrying a 4-byte fragment header. Simple commands (power, brightness) need no protobuf beyond a single SimpleMessage {i1} value. Re-verified against the same APK on 2026-08-08 (sha256 58aaf3d6027c59aa5ab7876930fb16661d224d28220f58f227e35c2ddeca07aa, fetched from the vendor's own CDN, http://file.daniaokeji.com/download/SmartDawn.apk).
DISCOVERY: advertised local name is 6-8 chars starting with "DN" (app-side filter, case-insensitive). The custom service UUID 00000074-1972-1925-3022-077119514e44 is what the official app's scan filter names, but the JY25CUT curtain controller tested live (2026-08-08, unit "DN0B88") does NOT include it in its advertisement — the ADV carries only the local name and a manufacturer-data record (company id 0x61ea + 12 payload bytes, observed 03 e8 00 64 14 14 00 00 72 74 00 00: fw_ver, factory id, product type, width, height, group, vendor, run-mode/leader flags). Scan matching must therefore key on the name prefix (and optionally the manufacturer data); the service UUID is confirmed from the GATT table after connecting.
WIFI VARIANTS: Daniao's platform also supports Wi-Fi control — same DDP framing over UDP port 4048, device presence announcements to app UDP port 14040, and AP-mode provisioning (controller AP "DN??????", password "00000000"; or phone hotspot named i5g*/I5G* with password "00000000"). Whether shipping SmartDawn-branded SKUs enable Wi-Fi is unverified; the curtain lights are BLE-per-listing.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for discovery, GATT layout, fragment framing, extended-header layout, and the core command path — code-sourced from two independent implementations inside the vendor's own app AND verified live against JY25CUT curtain hardware (unit "DN0B88", "DNX:S104-JY" per its DeviceInfo push) on 2026-08-08: connect + subscribe needs no pairing; the device immediately pushes M_DEVICE_INFO_NOTIFY (mt=2103) and a periodic M_PLAY_PROGRESS_NOTIFY (mt=2630) stream on the DDP notify characteristic; fragment-framed M_SET_POWEROFF/M_SET_POWERON commands (single-fragment, big-endian header fields) are acknowledged with M_POWER_STATUS_NOTIFY (mt=2105) and visibly pause/resume playback, while the SAME packets written WITHOUT the 4-byte fragment header are silently ignored — the framing is mandatory, not advisory. Commands worked without a prior M_TIME_SYNC. M_SET_BRIGHTNESS (mt=2509, protobuf SimpleMessage {i1}) is accepted without an ACK and the value echoes back in the next M_DEVICE_INFO_NOTIFY brightness field. The pixel-push path was also exercised live: M_DEV_START (mt=235) verifiably takes over the display (the M_PLAY_PROGRESS_NOTIFY stream goes silent until the mode is left), and full-canvas TUTU_RESTORE chunks then stream on the BIN channel (format under the BIN Write characteristic). M_GET_RUNNING_STATUS (mt=2104) produced no observable reply in that session (framed or not) — its semantics stay medium confidence, as does payload field usage for commands not exercised live (SimpleMessage i1/i2/s1 semantics, ranges), which follows app call sites. Header shape and UDP port 4048 echo the WLED/xLights DDP (Digital Display Protocol), suggesting a derivation, but the DNX extended channel is Daniao-specific.

credentials.notes: BLE path has no credentials. Wi-Fi provisioning (Wi-Fi SKUs only) uses the fixed AP/hotspot passphrase "00000000".

factory_reset.effect: M_FACTORY_RESET (mt=2598) and M_REBOOT (mt=2599) commands exist in the protocol. The controller hardware also has a physical mode button (per the FCC manual: press to switch mode, hold to turn off). No BLE bonding state exists to clear.

steps.action: Send M_FACTORY_RESET (mt=2598) over the DDP channel.
steps.expect: Device resets to factory state (per app code; not captured on hardware).

methods.description: Scan for a "DN"-prefixed name (6-8 chars) or the 00000074-1972-1925-3022-077119514e44 service UUID, connect, enable notifications on the DDP (01010074-...) and BIN (02010074-...) characteristics, request MTU, then send M_TIME_SYNC followed by normal commands.

steps.action: Power the lights; they advertise immediately.
Scan for the DN-prefixed name / 00000074-... service UUID and connect; subscribe to both notify characteristics and raise MTU.
Send M_TIME_SYNC (mt=2504, TimeSync protobuf) then command packets on the DDP write characteristic.

setup.notes: BLE models need no provisioning: power on, scan for the DN-prefixed name (the tested JY25CUT unit does not advertise the 00000074-... service UUID — see DISCOVERY), connect, subscribe to the DDP and BIN notify characteristics, negotiate MTU (app requests 512, payload MTU = negotiated - 3, fallback 20), then optionally send a time sync (M_TIME_SYNC, mt=2504) — the official app always does, but live testing (2026-08-08) confirmed power commands work without it. No pairing, bonding, or authentication on the command path — auth message types exist but serve cloud/sharing flows; the whole flow was exercised on JY25CUT curtain hardware over BlueZ. Wi-Fi SKUs (if any ship under SmartDawn) would use the AP-mode flow in the notes above (low confidence for this brand).

rejoin.notes: No bonding. Any central within range can connect and send commands.

variants.model: RGBIC permanent outdoor string lights (50/100/150/200 ft)
Smart icicle / net / meteor-shower / cone-tree / firecracker (HL1123) lights

characteristics.name: DDP Write
characteristics.notes: Command channel. Writes are BLE fragments (see service notes and the `framing` block: 4-byte [serial][total][remaining][tag=0] header on every write — MANDATORY, the device ignores unframed packets) whose reassembled payload is one DDP packet — usually a 20-byte extended (DNX) header plus optional protobuf payload. Responses arrive on the DDP notify characteristic.

characteristics.name: DDP Notify
characteristics.notes: Command responses and state pushes, reassembled with the same 4-byte fragment header. Notable inbound messages: M_DEVICE_INFO_NOTIFY (mt=2103, DeviceInfo protobuf with hardware, ports, capacity, colorOrder, chipType, fwVer, effects, productType, width, height), M_POWER_STATUS_NOTIFY (mt=2105), M_PLAY_INFO_NOTIFY (mt=2610), M_PLAY_PROGRESS_NOTIFY (mt=2630), M_NOTIFY_TWINKLE (mt=2597).

characteristics.name: BIN Write
characteristics.notes:
Bulk-data channel (same fragment framing, with a nonzero buffer tag in fragment-header byte 3). Two confirmed uses in v1.2.4: (1) file installs — effects, animations, layouts and other file payloads, M_START_INSTALL_* (mt 2901/2906/2915/2918/2921), *_PACKET, M_END_INSTALL_* flows; (2) live pixel push for the draw / photo-to-light modes, VERIFIED LIVE on JY25CUT curtain hardware 2026-08-08 (see the image_upload feature for the session sequence, which is M_UI_END_SYNC then M_DOODLE_START — NOT M_DEV_START, which blanks the canvas): after it, each full-canvas redraw is one or more TUTU_RESTORE (tag 4) buffer arrays with this exact layout (from the H5 bundle's TuTu.sendRecoveData, ported and exercised against hardware):
CHUNK = [start_x u8][start_y u8][palette_count u8 <= 16] + palette_count RGB triplets (the first <=16 distinct colors of the canvas in row-major scan order) + RLE pixel data. Pixels are traversed COLUMN-MAJOR (x outer, y inner); each run of identical palette indices encodes as one byte (index << 4) | run_length when run_length < 16, else (index << 4) followed by count bytes — 0xFF for each full 127, then the remainder byte. A chunk is flushed when header + pixel bytes reach 200; the next chunk's [start_x][start_y] is the coordinate where its first run began, and runs do NOT span a chunk boundary. Canvases with more than 16 distinct colors cannot be expressed — quantize first.
CRITICAL (verified live 2026-08-08): the device does NOT reassemble BLE fragments on this channel — it honors ONLY the first write of a TUTU transfer. So each CHUNK must be sent as a SINGLE BLE write; a chunk split across the 4-byte fragment framing renders only its first fragment (e.g. one strand of the image, rest blank). This is why the ~200-byte chunk cap and the large negotiated ATT MTU (app requests 527, device grants 512) matter: with MTU 512 every chunk fits one write. A full canvas may still be MANY chunks, each its own single-write transfer placed by its [start_x][start_y]; the device composites them. Sequential images and ~5fps animation work by re-sending chunks this way (M_DOODLE_START need not be resent per frame). Send M_UI_END_SYNC + M_DOODLE_START first, NOT M_DEV_START.
The live doodle path (finger drawing) instead sends TUTU_DOODLE (tag 1) deltas: [1][r][g][b] + a bit-run-length encoding of WHICH led indices changed to that one color (runs of skip/set with 7-bit counts, high bit = set). TUTU_ERASE=2 clears. Tag 16 (MUSIC_BIN) is defined in the H5 bundle alongside these but no call site was found.

characteristics.name: BIN Notify
characteristics.notes: Responses/progress for the BIN channel (e.g. M_INSTALL_EFFECTS_PACKET mt=2016 acknowledgements, M_UPLOAD_PROGRESS mt=2933).

characteristics.name: Uploader
characteristics.notes:
Bulk file-upload channel for BOTH firmware OTA and device-side STORAGE of effects/animations (persisted so they play standalone). The second UUID group is 2072 — unlike every other characteristic here, it does not share the 010x/020x-1972 pattern (confirmed in BleUtils5, SmartDawn 1.2.4 and BleUtils3, SuperPix 4.4.1).
STORAGE UPLOAD (decoded from an over-the-air capture 2026-08-08 and confirmed live — the handshake was replayed and the device ACKed): the whole transfer runs on THIS characteristic; the device answers on the DDP Notify characteristic. It does NOT use a DDP M_UPLOAD_START_REQUEST (2930) write.
  1. START packet (write here) = 8-byte header
     [id u8][packetnum u16 BE][0x11][0xFF][packetnum u16 BE]
     [crc8 over the WHOLE packet] followed by an UploadRequest
     protobuf {id=1, type=2 (0=effect .eff, 3=animation), size=3,
     offset=4 (0), packetnum=5=ceil(size/500), framesize=6 (500),
     crc8=7 (0), path=8 (omitted for animations), cid=9}.
  2. Device -> DDP Notify M_UPLOAD_START_RESPONSE (mt=2931),
     SimpleMessage: i1==0 accept (i1!=0 fail); i3 = resume byte
     offset (0 = start fresh). The device accepts a NOVEL cid, so
     custom content can be stored, not just re-installed catalog
     effects.
  3. DATA packets (write here) = 8-byte header
     [id][packetnum u16 BE][0x11][0xFF][remaining u16 BE]
     [crc8 over the PAYLOAD ONLY] + up to framesize (500) bytes;
     `remaining` counts down from packetnum-1 to 0. Payload is the
     "DN" AMX container (256-byte header + TinyProgram protobuf,
     CRC8 at header[9] over bytes 10.., padded to a 4096 multiple).
  4. Device -> DDP Notify M_UPLOAD_COMPLETE (mt=2934), i1==0 success;
     M_UPLOAD_PROGRESS (mt=2933) may stream during transfer. After
     success the app refreshes M_EFFECT_LIST (2904) and plays it via
     M_PLAY_EFFECT (2606) by cid.
CRC8 uses polynomial 0x97, MSB-first, init 0 — note the two DIFFERENT scopes (whole-packet for START, payload-only for DATA), both verified on the wire.
FIRMWARE OTA uses the same channel: M_START_UPDATE_FIRMWARE mt=2912, M_UPDATE_FIRMWARE_PACKET mt=2913, M_END_UPDATE_FIRMWARE mt=2914. Firmware binaries are fetched from https://daniaokeji.com/led/ota?<product,fw,...> which returns {code, fw:{version, desc, date, url}}.

services.name: Daniao DDP Service
services.notes:
Single custom GATT service carrying the whole protocol. Two logical channels: DDP (commands, DNX extended packets) and BIN (bulk/file data such as effect, animation, layout and firmware uploads), plus an uploader characteristic used in the firmware-update flow.
BLE FRAGMENT FRAMING (both channels): each logical packet is split into writes of at most the negotiated payload MTU (app requests ATT MTU 512, payload = MTU - 3, fallback 20). Every write carries a 4-byte fragment header: [message serial u8] [total fragments u8] [fragments remaining after this one u8, counts down to 0] [channel tag u8], followed by up to MTU-4 payload bytes. Reassembly keys on bytes 0-2. The tag byte is 0x00 on the DDP channel; on the BIN channel it identifies the buffer type — 1=TUTU_DOODLE (live doodle/ photo pixels), 2=TUTU_ERASE, 4=TUTU_RESTORE (full-canvas redraw), 16=MUSIC_BIN — read from the H5 bundle's B3 enum and BleUtils5.sendBinData. Writes use WRITE_TYPE_NO_RESPONSE (BleUtils5 sets write type 2 on the DDP writer).
EXTENDED (DNX) PACKET — the command format, 20-byte header: [0]=0xF0 (flag nibble 0xF, version 0), [1]=0x04 (from-role; app hardcodes 4=gateway), [2-3]=sn u16 BE, [4-5]=length u16 BE, [6-7]=mt (message type) u16 BE, [8-11]=cid u32 BE (0 from app), [12-13]=osn u16 BE, [14]=rcode u8 (0), [15]=ts u8 (random), [16-17]=csum u16 BE (app sends 0), [18-19]=0x00 0x00, followed by an optional protobuf payload. Default payload type is SimpleMessage { int32 i1=1; int32 i2=2; string s1=3; string s2=4; int32 i3=5; int32 i4=6; }.
STANDARD DDP PACKET (pixel/display data, datatype != 0xFF), 10-byte header: [0]=flag (PUSH=0x01, QUERY=0x02, REPLY=0x04, STORAGE=0x08, TIME=0x10, version bits 0xC0), [1]=sn u8, [2]=datatype (DISPLAY=0x01, DNX=0xE6, CONFIG=0xFA, STATUS=0xFB), [3]=target (app writes 0x01), [4-7]=offset u32 BE, [8-9]=psize u16 BE. Note: the app's dead Java Header.getBytes() writes offset little-endian while both live encoders (JS and decode path) treat it big-endian — BE is canonical. CAVEAT: the encoder for these packets (mkOrginDdp, flag 0xE1) ships in every Daniao H5 bundle checked (SmartDawn 1.2.4, SuperPix 4.4.1, legacy SmartPixels) but has NO call sites in any of them — the live pixel-push path in v1.2.4 is the BIN-channel doodle flow described on the BIN Write characteristic below. Treat DISPLAY-packet streaming as a dormant/ legacy capability until an on-air capture shows it in use.
Command templates below cover the 20-byte extended header; "{sn}" and "{payload}" are the variable parts. The templates do NOT include the 4-byte fragment header: each characteristic's `framing` block declares it machine-readably (scheme `daniao_fragment`), and encoders MUST apply it to every write — live testing (2026-08-08, JY25CUT curtain) confirmed the controller silently ignores unframed command packets and acknowledges framed ones. Multi-byte header fields (sn, len, cid, osn) are big-endian, declared per-parameter via `endianness`. WIRE-TRUTH (all four 2026-08 captures, every write to the DDP-write handle 0x0013): `len`=0, `osn`=0, `ts`=0, `cid`=0 for EVERY command — the header after mt is 12 zero bytes — with the SOLE exception of time_sync (mt=0x09C8), whose osn is 1. Earlier revisions filled `len` with packet_length and `osn` with 1; those bytes differed from the vendor on the wire (the tolerant device parsed them anyway), so the defaults are now 0 to match the captures byte-for-byte. `sn` is a per-message serial the encoder fills (`auto: sequence`; a constant 0 was also accepted on hardware).
